controls.requirement: Accessibility behavior is tested against the commissioned standard.
Critical user journeys and negative states have automated evidence.
Client performance is measured against a workload-specific budget.
API and event contracts are versioned and compatibility-tested.
Timeout, retry, idempotency, and dependency-failure paths are proven.
Requests carry end-to-end correlation and observable failure context.
Schema and data changes have forward, backward, and rollback evidence.
Constraints, isolation, retention, and deletion behavior are verified.
Backups are restored and measured against commissioned RPO and RTO.
Every protected operation enforces server-side authorization.
Cross-tenant read and write attempts fail at every relevant boundary.
Sessions, identities, keys, and deprovisioning have tested lifecycles.
Production promotion is staged, attributable, and approval-aware.
Deploy health and smoke behavior are measured in the target environment.
Rollback is tested against explicit triggers and time objectives.
Cloud topology is reviewable, reproducible, and drift-detected.
IAM, network, region, and secret boundaries are least-privilege.
Ownership, budgets, forecasts, and anomaly thresholds are explicit.
Required checks block unverified changes and overrides are auditable.
Dependencies, secrets, code, and infrastructure are scanned.
Release artifacts are attributable to source, build, and approval identity.
Assets, trust boundaries, threats, and mitigations are current.
Secrets are absent from source and use governed storage and rotation.
Known vulnerabilities are scanned, triaged, and remediated by SLA.
Limits are explicit by actor, tenant, endpoint, provider, and cost class.
Backoff, circuit breaking, and overload behavior avoid retry storms.
Usage and billing meters reconcile to authoritative records.
Cache keys include every identity, permission, version, and variation boundary.
Invalidation, freshness, and purge propagation are tested.
Personal or tenant data cannot cross cache boundaries.
Capacity and cost are tested against representative workload models.
Canary or progressive delivery has abort and rollback criteria.
Routing and scaling failure modes are exercised without unsafe blast radius.
Critical flows have correlated logs, metrics, and traces.
SLIs, SLOs, windows, alerts, and error budgets have named owners.
Telemetry excludes secrets and sensitive data and preserves audit integrity.
Availability, RTO, and RPO are workload-specific and windowed.
Restore, rollback, and failover are exercised and measured.
Incident roles, communication, evidence, and corrective actions are tested.
